t: Difference Between Maximum and Minimum Price Sum — Rerooting DP on Trees
o: We pick a root of the tree; the cost is (largest price-sum of a path starting at the root) − (smallest such sum). Since all prices are positive, the **minimum** path from any root is simply the root itself (extending only adds price), so min = price[root]. The maximum path from a root extends downward into the best child subtree. In example 1, rooting at node 2 gives max path 7+8+6+10 = 31 and min 7, cost 24. In example 2, rooting anywhere on the 3-chain gives 3 − 1 = 2. With n up to 1e5 we need an O(n) or O(n log n) tree DP, not trying every root naively.
k: Minimum path from a root is always just the root alone because prices are strictly positive.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute force re-rooting at every node
a.i: For each candidate root, run a DFS computing the deepest (maximum) downward price chain starting there; the answer for that root is that chain minus price[root]. Take the overall maximum. Correct but O(n²).
s: For each node r, DFS computing maxDown(r) = price[r] + max(0, max over children maxDown(child)).
Answer = max over r of maxDown(r) − price[r].
a.t: O(n²) — a full DFS per candidate root; too slow for n = 1e5 but conceptually clear.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency list and recursion stack.

a.n: Approach 2: Single DFS with downward DP (optimal)
a.i: Key observation: cost at root r = maxDown(r) − price[r], where maxDown(r) = price[r] + best downward chain into children. So we never need the 'up' direction at all — one post-order pass computing maxDown for every node suffices, and the answer is max over all nodes of maxDown(v) − price[v]. This works because choosing v as root makes its best path purely downward, and the min path is price[v].
s: Root the tree arbitrarily at node 0 and get a processing order iteratively (avoid deep recursion).
Process nodes in reverse order: down[p] = max(down[p], price[p] + down[child]).
a.t: O(n) — one iterative DFS pass over all nodes and edges.

w: In an interview, state the positivity observation first (min path = root alone), which collapses the problem to 'deepest downward chain over every choice of root', solvable with one tree DP. Pitfalls: recursion depth on a 1e5-node path tree (use iterative DFS), and forgetting the n = 1 edge case (answer 0, handled naturally since down[0] − price[0] = 0). Follow-ups: what if prices could be negative (then you'd need true max/min rerooting with top-2 child values); report the actual paths.
